title: Model Traffic Map & Interactive Spritepack for Pinning Quickstart
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Deliver a compact, interactive visual explainer (spritepack + micro-animations) for the Rollouts quickstart that demonstrates: 1) pinning a model version to a route, 2) creating a canary with traffic weighting, 3) A/B variant comparison, and 4) fallback policy behavior when capacity or latency thresholds are breached. The asset set should include annotated screenshots, an accessible SVG spritepack for small interactive previews in the docs, and a high-fidelity Figma prototype for the product team to drop into the console and onboarding flow.
screenshots_needed: Canary creation modal (compact): weight slider and preview badge
A/B variant compare screen: side-by-side output + quality markers
Fallback policy editor: chain view showing primary -> fallback -> degrade
Route page with pinned version chip and traffic distribution sparkline
Tooltip states for latency/cost badges on small screens
acceptance_criteria: Spritepack contains discrete frames for: idle, apply-pin, ramp-up, fallback-trigger, settle
All screenshots delivered at 1x and 2x PNG resolutions and annotated for engineering
Figma prototype demonstrates click-to-pin, weight drag, and simulated fallback with sample data
Docs-ready copy strings for each micro-state (max 140 chars) provided and reviewed by PM
Accessible SVGs include title/desc elements and pass color-contrast checks
Assets uploaded to Drive and referenced in Console PR with export checklist
comments: 2026-03-01 - Kickoff: scoped interactive spritepack to ~6 frames to keep bundle small for docs embedding. PM (Evan Cole) asked for explicit latency threshold state in fallback animation.
2026-03-03 - Early mock review: Eng (Priya Nambiar) requested that the canary preview include a synthetic QPS badge so users can correlate weight with expected throughput; added to requirements.
2026-03-05 - Design review: added reduced-motion variant and ensured microcopy aligns with localization guidance (LU table started in Confluence).
2026-03-08 - QA pass: accessibility checks fail for one orange-on-white badge — updated color to meet WCAG 2.1 AA; noted in handoff PDF.
2026-03-10 - PM feedback: prefer 'traffic pin' phrasing over 'version lock' in quickstart copy; updated strings and prototype.
Next steps: finalize spritepack exports, hand off to eng for console integration ticket ENG-48210, and add animated preview to docs home page via markdown embed.
review_feedback: PM Evan Cole: tighten the onboarding flow — the interactive preview should run on a loop no longer than 6s and have a single CTA example (pin->canary->fallback).
Eng Priya Nambiar: confirm SVG exports are optimized (minified, id-unique) and provide separate reduced-motion assets for users with prefers-reduced-motion.
Security: forward assets to infra-security for quick check if any URLs in mock data reference internal hostnames (done).
Localization: content owner to provide translations for three priority locales (en, fr, de) once copy is finalized.
decision_log: Decision 2026-03-02: Keep the spritepack small (<= 8 frames) for faster docs load; use CSS-driven interpolation for weight changes to reduce frame count.
Decision 2026-03-06: Use a heatmap overlay on the traffic map to visualize latency hotspots instead of numerical latency-only badges to make state transitions more visually intuitive.
